title: The RISC-V ABI, and the Register That Isn't There
description: Pass arguments and results the way RISC-V code requires, and understand why the architecture needs no condition-code register at all -- and what a compiler does instead.
author: Underlayer
completion_criteria: Read all 4 concepts, reproduce the 171 checks in courses/rvabi/assets/samples/crosscheck.py against the shipped rvabi.out, then break one of the four numbers a poison claims -- remove a prepended correction, or break the two-bit length rule -- and watch the delta move by name. The two-bit `(\\S+)` in the m18 check was a real harness bug and is documented where it was fixed.

modules.title: The Contract: What Two Compilers Agree On
The Absence: What Is Missing, and What It Buys

concepts.title: The Calling Convention
concepts.description: a0-a7 for integers, fa0-fa7 for doubles, a0 and fa0 for the return value, s0-s11 preserved across a call, t0-t6 and a0-a7 not, ra and sp privileged, and the first stacked argument at offset ZERO because there is no return address on the stack to skip. Measured against the specification, not quoted: 44 of 44 register-resident integer argument placements agree at -O2, read out of the RELOCATION each store carries rather than out of a text file. The row no summary gets right is the ninth DOUBLE -- with fa0-fa7 exhausted it goes to a0, an INTEGER register, and f9 reads no stack argument at any level, because the hardware floating-point convention falls back to the integer one. And m18, nine integers then nine doubles, is the case that decides whether there is one counter or two: two, and the ninth double is at 8(sp) because the ninth integer took 0(sp).

concepts.title: No Flags Register, No Condition Codes, No CMOV
concepts.description: The section's spine, and the manual admits the decision in its own words: 'We considered but did not include conditional moves or predicated instructions, which can effectively replace unpredictable short forward branches.' So the absence is a documented choice, not an inference from a hole. MEASURED over eleven functions of `?:` at four optimisation levels: the compiler picks a BRANCH for most of the corpus, reaches for ARITHMETIC only where arithmetic is cheaper, and emits no CMOVcc and no SETcc because neither exists. And the half nobody states: because sltu WRITES A REGISTER, `(x < 0) ? 1 : 0` is ONE instruction -- `srliw a0, a0, 31` -- where x86-64 would need a SETL that does not exist. The three targets' idioms are 17 branches, 16 csel/cneg and 16 cmov, and the three sets are DISJOINT, computed pairwise and printed.

concepts.title: The Register File as Roles, Not Numbers
concepts.description: The ABI names ROLES: t0 is x5, s0 is x8 and is also called fp, ra is x1, sp is x2, zero is x0, and gp and tp are UNALLOCATABLE -- a stronger word than preserved, measured at 0 writes across the whole corpus. x0 is hardwired to zero, so `li zero, 42` ASSEMBLES to four real bytes and the discard is a property of silicon this host does not have. And there are two register FILES, not one: `fsd fa0, -24(s0)` names one register in each, the same five bits, and a reader that picks the wrong file reports a real register of the wrong kind with no other symptom. Which is why the census is preceded by its own audit: 5,973 instructions checked against a second rendering, and the first version of this reader answered 'which file' once per instruction and got 18 writes to gp over a corpus with none.

concepts.title: What Compression Does to the ABI and to Disassembly
concepts.description: `rvasm`'s concept 3 already measured the ENCODING; this measures the CONSEQUENCE. A spill: 11 instructions and 44 bytes become 11 and 26. A call/return pair: 4 and 16 become 4 and 10. And the methodological result that matters more than either: `rv64i` against `rv64gc` is CONFOUNDED -- it also removes F and D, so every `double` becomes a soft-float CALL, and the -38 it reports is the library and not the encoding. The clean pair is `rv64imafd` against `rv64imafdc`, and there the instruction delta is +0, +0 and +6: the C extension changes how many BYTES an operation takes and almost never how many operations. Then the boundary problem, which is rvdec.py's central problem and this section's: instructions are 2 or 4 bytes, so you cannot find a boundary by knowing the length, only by reading two bits of the current position -- 6,048 instructions found by the rule against 5,012 with the length handed in.
